:::{#rem-matmul-not-commutative}
#### Matrix multiplication is not commutative

When $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ and $\matr{B}\matr{A}$ are both defined,
they are usually different.
For example, with

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{A}\matr{B}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
\matr{B}\matr{A}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix},
\end{aligned}
$$

so $\matr{A}\matr{B} \neq \matr{B}\matr{A}$.

:::
